label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: Part one is final, and nothing misses it: I flagged it ready for its lock.
findings.why: The opening conductor speech uses lock, flag and part before any is explained (the glossary comes at line 45), and 'nothing misses it' is opaque, so a first reader stalls at the top of the chapter.

findings.quote: In its last hour, the team was doing what it had done all afternoon, only faster.
findings.why: The narrator reports the team from outside with no 'I' and no hindsight, where the editor could say what he saw from the player.

findings.quote: Deck put the title slide in front of it. The storyteller checked parts two and three
findings.why: Quoted dialogue for the conductor is shown as speech and only marked Dramatised after the scene, so a reader who cares about sources takes invented lines as record until the tag arrives.

findings.quote: four hundred and thirty-nine commits by the agents, a hundred and sixty-two sessions on the record
findings.why: The scene reads the tally aloud and the figure at line 91 then draws the same tally; as a sourcing-minded reader I also want the register id beside a number this prominent.

findings.quote: The thing that actually stopped the factory came from outside it: me, deciding that the day's work was done.
findings.why: The reason for stopping was already told at line 49 and is told again in chapter 17 line 11, so the same account appears three times.

findings.quote: what is left is the accounting, at full size: the failures stay in.
findings.why: The same promise is made again at line 24 (The failures stay in, at full size), so the reader hears it twice within twenty lines.

findings.quote: Chapter 16 told this one. In a line:
findings.why: The lock is retold here as narration and then a third time in the two dev lines that follow, after it filled most of chapter 16.

findings.quote: The conductor asked the storyteller to split the story into three parts by a deadline in the late afternoon.
findings.why: A narrator line that reports the record with no 'I' and no hindsight, repeated across the cards (lines 44, 111, 123) so the card format reads like a log.

findings.quote: it was nothing sensitive, an agent that got a bit excited
findings.why: As an editor who needs sources I would stop here: data from other sites went into a public push, and the text waves it away with no description of what it was or how it was checked.

findings.quote: One was in the article only, one on no beat or slide at all, one in the story tree only.
findings.why: Article, beat and story tree are used as if known and the three claims are never named, so the reader cannot see which claims failed.

findings.quote: Not a disaster on stage. A small, true error that the record caught and the freeze kept in.
findings.why: Two clipped fragments that could run into one sentence with the thought that the record caught it.

findings.quote: the first wake to follow it was the wake that wrote it.
findings.why: Wake is used from the first lines and only defined at line 19, and pre-review and post-review appear before the stages are laid out.

findings.quote: The first wake in the record that the clock started, and not me, is not the conductor's.
findings.why: A double negative that I had to read twice before I knew whose wake it was.

findings.quote: And not only for the member that skipped. For every member.
findings.why: Fragments that could join the previous sentence so it keeps its thought.

findings.quote: Plan it, have the plan checked, do it, have it checked, check it went to plan.
findings.why: The five stages are listed here, explained at line 13, and walked through again step by step, and the Something to try repeats the point about a record you know is wrong.

findings.quote: every piece of work on the team went the same way, and a skipped step stopped the release
findings.why: In this chapter the editor's signature as a control is not shown, only reviewers who are the same kind of agent, and a reader worried about a rubber-stamping editor wants to see where he signs.

what_holds: 16-hour-nineteen-minute-by-minute.md: the hold file quoted as written and the plain admission that the 95% was a coincidence; a stop button that stops the next session and not one already running is the finding I would take away.
17-what-did-not-work.md: each failure is a card with its cost and whose record says so, which is the discipline I want in my own newsroom; the freeze and the key rotation read as honest.
07-hour-three-the-five-steps.md: the walk through one real wake record, including the review catching its own author, shows the check working and not only being described.
notes: The prose itself is mostly clean. For the newsroom question, the clearest gap is where the editor signs as a control: chapters 16 and 7 show agents checking agents, and the editor appears as the person who stops, not yet as the person who signs.
